govdocs-archive_org-nciplesOfTopological: Kurt Lewin’s Principles of Topological Psychology — 1936 — sets out his field theory of human behavior. The great Gestalt psychologist’s work reshaped social psychology. Life space is his key concept. The math daunts but rewards. The book remains a classic of the field.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-in-li: A 1913 entry on Abraham in the liturgy — how the Church's prayers honor the patriarch. Hugh Henry gathers the texts and chants. His bosom holds the blessed dead. Prayer-book Abraham, through the ages. The Requiem Mass still sings of Abraham's bosom.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-african-litur: This 1913 reference piece on the African liturgy — the lost rite of Carthage and Hippo. John Goggin rebuilds it from fragments. Augustine prayed these very words. The Vandals swept the rite away. A vanished worship, lovingly restored. Its psalm tones survive in the old books.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agnus-dei-in-: A 1913 entry on the Agnus Dei in the liturgy — the Lamb of God in Mass and chant. Hugh Henry traces its sacred use. Threefold mercy falls on the altar. The faithful sing it kneeling. The Mass's tenderest prayer. Its plea ends every Mass on earth.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-in-litu: This 1913 reference piece on the altar in the liturgy — its meaning and consecration. Augustin Schulte treats the holy table. Christ Himself is the true altar. Bishops anoint its stone with chrism. The Church's sacred center. Its kiss begins the priest's Mass.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-analogy: A 1913 entry on analogy in philosophy — the middle way of knowing God. George Sauvage explains the doctrine. We speak of God neither wholly same nor wholly other. The schools built on this bridge. Reason's path to the divine. Its ladder climbs from earth to heaven.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anatole-de-be: This 1913 reference piece on Anatole de Bengy — the Jesuit martyr of the Paris Commune. Dennis Kavanagh honors his death. He died blessing his murderers in 1871. The Church counts him among its martyrs. A priest of the barricades' fury. His beatification crowned the martyrs' cause.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antiochene-li: This 1913 reference piece on the Antiochene liturgy — the rite of the Syrian East. Adrian Fortescue unfolds its ancient form. St. James's liturgy is its crown. The East prays in its solemn tones. The mother rite of the Orient. Its anaphora is the oldest in use.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antiphon-in-g: A 1913 entry on the antiphon in the Greek liturgy — the psalm's refrain. Henri Leclercq explains its Eastern form. The choirs answer verse with verse. The liturgy moves on their wings. The East's sung dialogue. Their melodies are ancient and solemn.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostle-in-li: A 1913 entry on the Apostle in liturgy — the book of the Epistles. Andrew Shipman explains its Eastern use. The reader chants the apostolic word. The liturgy hears Paul's voice. The East's book of the Epistle. Its pages are richly illuminated.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-archaeology: A 1913 entry on Christian archaeology — the science of the Church's stones. Patrick Connellan surveys its vast field. The catacombs are its richest mine. The monuments confirm the written word. The spade in the Church's service. Its finds fill the Lateran museum.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ascetical-the: This 1913 reference article on ascetical theology — the science of Christian perfection. Franz Xaver Mutz sets out its classic method. The soul climbs by prayer and denial. The masters mapped the interior way. The textbook of the spiritual life. Its masters fill the spiritual shelves.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-assemblies-of: This 1913 reference piece on the Assemblies of the French Clergy — the Gallican convocations. Jean Auguste Sicard tells their proud story. They voted the Church's gift to the king. The old regime heard their voice. The clergy's parliament of France. Their don gratuit filled the royal coffers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-astrology: This 1913 reference piece on astrology — the Church's judgment of the star readers. Maximilian Jacobi treats its history. The stars incline, they do not compel. The Church condemns the fatalist art. A superstition, judged by faith. Its charts still tempt the curious.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benefit-of-cl: A 1913 entry on benefit of clergy — the cleric's escape from the secular court. Richard Burtsell traces its medieval privilege. The neck verse saved the reader. The law at last abolished the plea. The Church's ancient immunity. Its plea saved the literate felon.
